meta.tagline: One week lost, nothing broken. Eight weeks to go — the long runs that matter are still ahead.
meta.overviewDeck: 16-week build from 15 km to race day, recalibrated on Oct 11 from the Aug–Oct watch data.
meta.zonesDeck: Heart-rate targets drive every workout on the watch. Paces below are what those heart rates produced in Aug–Oct.
meta.revisionNote: Week 8 (Oct 5–11) was lost to a business trip and illness. It takes the place of the recovery week that was scheduled next, so week 9 becomes an easy return week, the missed 26 km with a marathon-pace finish moves to Oct 24, the 30 km follows on Oct 31, and the 32 km peak and 3-week taper stay where they were. Goal pace moves from 6:20 to ~6:00/km (≈4:13): the last 4 km of the 24 km ran 5:48–5:51/km. The marathon-pace heart-rate band drops to 145–158 so Thursday sessions line up with that pace.

foundation.notes: Consistent training since June 1. One week lost (Oct 5–11) to a business trip and illness.

currentForm.consistency: Very good — one missed week in nineteen
currentForm.notes: 24 km on Oct 3 at 6:14/km average, HR ~150; last 4 km at 5:48–5:51/km (HR 154–160). Pace-to-heart-rate drift stayed at or under ~4% on all seven long runs of 15–24 km since mid-August.

strengths.evidence: Aerobic durability: pace-to-HR drift ≤4% on every long run from 15 to 24 km
Finished the 24 km with 4 km at 5:48–5:51/km — about 30 s/km faster than the Rev 3 goal pace
Tempo reps at ~5:05/km and MP reps at 5:15–5:35/km, all inside their heart-rate bands
Easy-run efficiency up ~8% from June to September; ground contact time down from ~310 to ~265 ms

limiters.evidence: Four strength sessions logged since June — still the main injury risk as the long run goes to 32 km
Never beyond 24 km. At km 17–19 of the 24 km, HR rose to 153–159 while pace slipped to 6:29–6:35 — fuelling and durability to test at 26 and 30 km
Returning from 8 days off (travel + illness); the first week back has to be easy

constraints: 9-to-5 work, business travel + two children (1 yo & 11 yo)
Rolling dune terrain near the coast — hillier than the flat Valencia course

hr.notes: Max HR 188 (observed 185 on strides). Tempo reps held 166–168 for 10 minutes, consistent with LTHR ~170. Marathon band lowered in Rev 4 to 145–158.

zones.name: Marathon
zones.feels: Steady, full sentences — race HR until km 30

pace.notes: From Aug–Oct runs at the stated heart rates. Goal pace is confirmed by the marathon-pace finishes of the 26 km (Oct 24) and 30 km (Oct 31).

phases.name: Build
phases.focus: Tempo + MP work, long run to 24 km

workouts.name: Strength B — Core & Stability
workouts.description: Core + single-leg balance. Protects form when you fatigue late in long runs.
workouts.humanReadable:
Warm-up (5 min): cat-cow, bird-dog 2x8
Main (3 rounds, 45s rest):
  • Plank — 30–45s
  • Side plank — 20–30s each side
  • Dead bug — 8 each side
  • Single-leg deadlift — 8 each leg
  • Step-ups onto chair — 10 each leg
Cool-down (5 min): pigeon stretch, child's pose

workouts.name: Easy + 5 Strides — 45 min
workouts.description: Easy aerobic plus short pickups to hold leg speed and high cadence.
workouts.humanReadable:
Warm-up: 15 min easy
Main: 20 min easy
Strides: 5 x 20s acceleration to ~5K effort, 60s walk between
Cool-down: 5 min easy

workouts.name: Easy Run — 35 min (optional 4th run)
workouts.description: Optional. Run only if recovery is good — skip freely on bad-sleep weeks.
workouts.humanReadable:
OPTIONAL — only if you feel fresh.
Warm-up: 5 min
Main: 25 min very easy (HR <145)
Cool-down: 5 min

Tired, poor sleep, or any knee signal? Do mobility instead.

workouts.name: Easy Run — 45 min
workouts.description: Easy/conversational. HR 135–148. Let pace be whatever that allows.
workouts.humanReadable:
Warm-up: 5 min very easy
Main: 35 min easy (HR 135–148, ~6:30–7:00/km)
Cool-down: 5 min easy + stretch

workouts.name: Strength A — Lower Body Foundation
workouts.description: Knee insurance. Single-leg & glute work. Critical now that long runs pass 20 km.
workouts.humanReadable:
Warm-up (5 min): leg swings, hip circles, glute bridges 2x10
Main (3 rounds, 60s rest):
  • Bodyweight squats — 12 reps
  • Reverse lunges — 8 each leg
  • Single-leg glute bridges — 10 each leg
  • Calf raises — 15 reps
  • Side-lying clamshells — 12 each side
Cool-down (5 min): hip flexor & quad stretches

workouts.name: 🏁 VALENCIA MARATHON 42.2 km
workouts.description: RACE DAY! See Race Strategy tab.
workouts.humanReadable: Goal ~6:00/km (≈4:13). First 10 km at 6:05–6:10 — deliberately held back. Settle into 6:00 from km 10 with HR ≤158. From km 32, press only if HR is still ≤160. Walk aid stations to fuel cleanly. Gel at km 7, then every 5 km. The training is in your legs.

pacing.strategy: Controlled negative split — hold back early, press late

firstHalf.notes: Deliberately slower than goal. HR ~145–150. It will feel too easy — that is right.

secondHalf.notes: Keep HR ≤158 until km 30. If it climbs, ease off 5–10 s/km — that is fine.

segments.cue: Hold back. HR ~145–150. Too easy is correct.
HR ≤158. Fuel on schedule even if you don't feel like it.
Press only if HR is still ≤160 and legs are good. Otherwise hold.

pacing.lastTenK: Press only if HR is still ≤160 at km 32. Otherwise hold 6:00.
pacing.warnings: Your long runs already average ~6:10 at HR ~148, so 6:00 will feel easy early. That feeling is the trap: a 6:08 first 10 km costs you about a minute; a 5:45 first 10 km can cost you fifteen after km 35.

nutrition.preRace: Night before: pasta + lean protein, nothing new. 3 hr before: ~100g carbs (oatmeal, banana, honey, low fibre). Coffee 60 min before if usual.

during.schedule: Gel at km 7 (~40 min), then every 5 km: 7/12/17/22/27/32/37. ~25 g each, always with water. Walk the aid stations to drink properly.
during.products: Only what you have practised in long runs.

nutrition.rule: Nothing new on race day. The 26 km and 30 km are your last two full fuel rehearsals.

raceMorning.gear: Only what you have trained in. New shoes = blisters.

mentalCues: Km 1–10: 'Too easy. Good. That's the plan.'
Km 11–21: 'Rhythm. Drink. Fuel. Relax the shoulders.'
Km 22–32: 'Now the race starts. Quick feet, tall posture.'
Km 33–42: 'Everyone hurts now. The 32 km run is in my legs. One km at a time.'

postRace.immediate: Keep walking 10 min. Electrolytes. Eat within 30 min.
postRace.next72hrs: Light walking only. No running. Sleep.
postRace.return: First easy jog 5–7 days after. Two unstructured weeks before any structure.

coachingNotes: 📋 REVISION 4 (Oct 11): One week lost to a business trip and illness. It replaces the recovery week that was due next, so the cost is one session — the 26 km with a marathon-pace finish — which moves to Oct 24. The 32 km peak (Nov 14) and the 3-week taper are unchanged. Don't try to make up the missed miles.

🤒 Return rule for week 9: run only if the fever is gone and any symptoms are above the neck (stuffy nose, mild sore throat). Chest symptoms, fever or body aches mean another rest day. If HR on an easy pace sits 5+ beats above normal, shorten the run.

🎯 Goal pace moves 6:20 → ~6:00/km (≈4:13). The last 4 km of the 24 km ran 5:48–5:51/km at HR 154–160, and MP sessions on fresh legs ran 5:15–5:35/km. It stays provisional: the MP finishes of the 26 km and 30 km decide between ~5:50 (4:06) and ~6:10 (4:20).

❤️ Marathon-pace HR band lowered to 145–158 (was 152–162). With the old band, Thursday MP work came out at 5:15–5:35/km — race effort, but well faster than race pace. The new band lines up with ~6:00/km.

⛽ On the 24 km, HR crept to 153–159 at km 17–19 while pace slipped to 6:29–6:35, then km 20 was slow and the finish was strong. That pattern often means carbs ran low. On the 26 and 30 km: first gel at 40–45 min, then every 30 min, no skipping.

💪 STRENGTH IS STILL THE GAP. Four sessions logged since June. The long run is about to go from 24 to 32 km. Monday and Friday, 25–30 minutes — the single-leg work is what keeps the knee quiet under that load.
🏃 Long runs average HR 146–150, at the top of the easy band. Keep the first half at 148 or below; the drift in the second half is where the training effect is.
📈 Fitness since May: easy-run efficiency up ~8% (June → September), ground contact time down from ~310 to ~265 ms, pace-to-HR drift ≤4% on every long run.
⛰️ Valencia is flat; your long runs are not (the 18 km on Aug 29 had ~200 flights of climbing). Flat-course race pace should come out a little quicker than your training numbers.
⌚ The duplicate 'Indoor Run' records stopped after Sep 12, so training load is no longer double-counted.
🧪 Next checkpoint: after the 30 km on Oct 31. Export then and we lock race pace.
